2.draft_content:
This engagement covers the implementation of SAP Cloud ALM for Metro from January 2026 through October 2026 to enable Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management in alignment with the S/4 RISE migration plan. The scope includes SAP Cloud ALM tenant setup, standard change management configuration, monitoring, alerting and dashboard capabilities, and transition to the METRO team, with go-live targeted for September 2026 and hypercare through October 2026.

- Establish SAP Cloud ALM for Metro’s landscape, including tenant setup, data flow configuration, user management, and monitoring foundations.
- Configure Technical Monitoring and standard Change Request Management, including dashboards, alerting, transport routes, and release strategies aligned to the S/4 migration program.
- Enable operational transition to the METRO team through end-to-end testing, train-the-trainer activities, SOP handover, and hypercare support.

Deferred decisions, assumptions, and any open dependencies are captured in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.draft_content:
### 3.1 Background
Metro is implementing SAP Cloud ALM to support its S/4 RISE migration and replace legacy ALM processes with a standardized cloud-based model. The engagement focuses on Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management, including tenant setup, monitoring and alerting, dashboard enablement, transport governance, and transition to the METRO team.

Metro’s current challenge is to align operational monitoring and change control with the migration timeline while covering a hybrid landscape that includes SAP S/4HANA Cloud, BTP applications, MII, Datasphere, Ariba, and Integration Suite. The business drivers are to reduce migration effort, establish end-to-end visibility across systems and integrations, improve release and transport control, and enable faster issue detection and response through standard SAP Cloud ALM capabilities.

### 3.2 Objectives
- Establish SAP Cloud ALM tenant and required connectivity for Metro’s in-scope landscape.
- Implement Technical Monitoring capabilities for system health, jobs, users, integrations, alerts, and dashboards.
- Configure standard SAP Cloud ALM Change Request Management aligned to Metro’s transport governance model.
- Support Dev and QA change-cycle setup and end-to-end testing before production deployment.
- Align Cloud ALM delivery milestones with the S/4 RISE migration plan and September 2026 go-live.
- Train Metro users and prepare SOPs to enable transition to the METRO team in October 2026.

### 3.3 Indicative To-Be Process Flow
In the target state, Metro will use SAP Cloud ALM as the central platform for operational monitoring and standard change management across the in-scope SAP landscape. Technical signals from connected systems and integrations will feed Cloud ALM for health monitoring, job monitoring, user performance monitoring, integration monitoring, and alert management. In parallel, change requests will follow a defined workflow with configured transport routes, release strategies, and dashboard visibility from development through quality and production deployment.

<IMAGE id="bc2c9706ab7b"/>

The implementation sequence is planned as pre-project and preparation in January 2026, prepare from February to April 2026, explore in May 2026, realize from June to September 2026, deployment in September 2026, and hypercare and transition in October 2026. The end state is a live SAP Cloud ALM setup with monitoring and ChaRM capabilities in operation, trained Metro users, and support transitioned to the METRO team.

### 4.1 Geographical Scope
Services will be delivered for Metro’s SAP Cloud ALM implementation supporting the S/4 RISE migration program across the Metro landscape identified for this engagement. In scope are the client environments and teams participating in the January 2026 to October 2026 implementation, including non-production and production landscapes required for Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management. Delivery may be performed through Bristlecone onshore and offshore teams in alignment with the agreed project governance, while system coverage is limited to the Metro SAP landscape and connected platforms listed in this Statement of Work.

### 4.2 Process Scope
In scope are the processes required to establish SAP Cloud ALM for operations and change enablement aligned to the S/4 RISE migration plan, including:
- SAP Cloud ALM standard change management
- Change cycle setup for development, quality, and production transport flow
- Transport route and release strategy configuration
- End-to-end change cycle testing for the first wave of changes
- System health monitoring
- Application monitoring
- Job and automation monitoring
- User performance monitoring for S/4HANA
- Integration and exception monitoring
- Notification and alert management
- Monitoring dashboard setup
- Support transition and knowledge transfer to the Metro team

### 4.3 Technical Scope
Technical scope includes SAP Cloud ALM tenant setup, onboarding, prerequisite configuration, and enablement of data flows from Metro systems into SAP Cloud ALM. Scope covers configuration of monitoring use cases, alerting, dashboards, user management, and ChaRM-related transport governance within SAP Cloud ALM standard capabilities. Technical coverage includes SAP S/4HANA Cloud, SAP BTP applications, MII, SAP Datasphere, SAP Ariba, and integrations through CPI / SAP Integration Suite where required for the agreed monitoring and change scenarios. Production mapping in ChaRM workflow and production inclusion in monitoring use cases are in scope during deploy and hypercare.

<IMAGE id="410e29befe04"/>

Included services are:
- Project management and coordination with Metro governance and project teams
- SAP Cloud ALM solution design aligned to the S/4 RISE migration plan
- Tenant onboarding and landscape readiness assessment
- Configuration of Technical Monitoring use cases
- Configuration of standard Change Request Management workflows
- Setup of transport routes, release strategies, and transport sequence mapping
- Setup of alerting, notifications, dashboards, and issue resolution support
- End-to-end testing support for agreed change cycles and monitoring scenarios
- Train-the-trainer workshop delivery
- SOP preparation for end users
- Deploy support, hypercare support, and transition to the Metro team

5.draft_content:
The solution will use SAP Cloud ALM as the central SaaS application lifecycle management platform for Metro’s S/4 RISE migration, covering Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management within a single tenant subaccount. The architecture is designed to connect Metro’s in-scope SAP landscape and integration flows to Cloud ALM for monitoring, alerting, dashboarding, and controlled transport governance.

<IMAGE id="a9602c43b0d1"/>

The deployment model is SAP-hosted on SAP BTP, with Metro systems and integrations configured to send operational and monitoring data to SAP Cloud ALM for system health, application, job, user performance, and integration monitoring. The target landscape includes SAP S/4HANA Cloud, BTP applications, MII, Datasphere, Ariba, and Integration Suite components that are in scope for onboarding and data-flow configuration.

The change-governance structure will use SAP Cloud ALM standard Change Request Management with configured workflows, transport routes, release strategies, and transport sequencing across DEV, QA, and PROD. The governance model will support multiple change types, approval-driven status progression, end-to-end testing of the first change cycle, and controlled transition of ongoing operations to the Metro team after deploy and hypercare.

The Cloud ALM Architect will define and implement the solution architecture in coordination with Bristlecone project management, the S/4 lead, and Metro’s project governance team. Metro will provide a single point of contact for ChaRM inputs, core-team support for cycle testing, and the required landscape, role, and monitoring-use-case inputs needed to complete configuration.

### 6.1 Implementation Methodology
The engagement will be delivered in phased alignment with Metro’s S/4 RISE migration plan, covering SAP Cloud ALM tenant onboarding, Technical Monitoring enablement, Change Request Management configuration, deployment, and transition to the Metro team.

<IMAGE id="57aeb9cf761c"/>

The implementation methodology is:
- **Pre-Project / Discover + Prepare:** confirm SAP Cloud ALM subscription, onboard the technical team, identify the target landscape, and finalize connectivity planning for in-scope use cases.
- **Prepare / Explore & Design:** validate user and role matrix, finalize monitoring use cases and metric values, define the target transport governance model, and complete prerequisite configuration readiness.
- **Realize — Technical Monitoring:** configure health, job, user performance, integration, exception, alerting, and notification monitoring for agreed systems and dashboards.
- **Realize — ChaRM:** configure standard change management workflow, transport routes, and release strategies, and execute the first end-to-end Dev and QA change cycle.
- **Deploy / Hypercare:** integrate production into ChaRM and monitoring use cases, support issue resolution, update operating documents, deliver train-the-trainer and SOP materials, and transition support to the Metro team.

Delivery will be led by the Bristlecone Cloud ALM Architect working with the Metro project team and S/4 workstream stakeholders. The methodology assumes timely availability of landscape details, finalized monitoring use cases, authorization inputs, and transition stakeholders.

### 16.1 Milestone Deliverables Matrix
Milestone deliverables shall align to the deliverables listed in Section 9 and the commercial terms in Section 13. Each milestone will be considered complete only when the related deliverables, acceptance criteria, and responsible sign-off party are defined and documented. Invoicing shall follow achievement and acceptance of the applicable milestone deliverables rather than elapsed time alone.

The milestone structure for this engagement is:
- Pre-Project / Discover + Prepare — Cloud ALM value proposition and scope document, connectivity plan for use cases, Cloud ALM onboarding documentation
- Prepare / Explore & Design — landscape readiness, prerequisite note implementation and configuration, data flow setup between SAP systems and SAP Cloud ALM, transport sequence mapping
- Realize — Health Monitoring, Job and Automation Monitoring, User Performance Monitoring, Integration and Exception Monitoring, alerting and notification setup, monitoring dashboard
- Realize (ChaRM) — configured change management workflow, transport routes and release strategies, first wave of change cycle tested end-to-end for Dev and QA, train-the-trainer workshop, SOP for end users
- Deploy / Hypercare — production system mapping in ChaRM workflow, production monitoring use cases enabled, issue resolution, document updates, and transition support to the METRO team

### 16.2 Deferred Scope Decisions
- Final monitoring use cases and metric thresholds must be frozen before Realize activities start.
- User and role matrix for SAP Cloud ALM must be approved before authorization configuration and testing.
- Target transport governance model must be finalized before ChaRM workflow and release strategy configuration.
- Transition plan, stakeholder ownership, and METRO support model must be confirmed before Deploy and Hypercare.
- Any requested expansion beyond the defined SAP Cloud ALM Technical Monitoring and Change Request Management scope will be handled through change control.

### 16.3 Integration & Custom Code Safeguards
- Integration scope is limited to the landscapes and interfaces identified for SAP S/4HANA Cloud, BTP applications, MII, and Integration Suite within the agreed scope.
- Data flow configuration, monitoring setup, and alerting will be based on the systems, use cases, and integration technologies confirmed during onboarding and design.
- Any additional systems, interfaces, monitoring scenarios, dashboard requirements, or reporting needs identified after scope baseline approval may affect effort, timeline, and commercials.
- ChaRM configuration will use standard SAP Cloud ALM change management capabilities unless otherwise agreed through approved change control.
- Custom development, bespoke extensions, and non-standard workflows are excluded unless expressly stated in Section 4 or added through an approved change request.
- Production cutover support depends on successful go-live readiness of the relevant landscapes and transport migration prerequisites.

### 16.4 Change Control
All scope, schedule, deliverable, and commercial changes shall be managed through the Change Management Process set out in Section 17. No out-of-scope work, additional integration enablement, non-standard configuration, or timeline adjustment will proceed without documented impact assessment and formal approval. Deviations from agreed assumptions, milestone dependencies, or client obligations that affect delivery shall also be routed through Section 17 for evaluation and disposition.

### 19.1 Termination for Convenience
Either party may terminate this Statement of Work for convenience by giving the other party <LEGAL: notice period for termination for convenience> prior written notice. Either party may terminate this Statement of Work immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this Statement of Work and fails to cure that breach within the applicable cure period under the governing agreement. Either party may also terminate immediately if the other party becomes insolvent, enters liquidation or bankruptcy proceedings, ceases to do business in the ordinary course, or commits fraud, wilful misconduct, or a material violation of applicable law in connection with the Services. On termination or expiry, Bristlecone will cease the terminated Services, provide Metro with completed deliverables and agreed project materials prepared through the termination date, and support an orderly handover of SAP Cloud ALM implementation artifacts then in scope, including transition items relevant to handoff to the METRO team. Metro will pay all undisputed fees and approved expenses for Services performed through the termination date, including approved work-in-progress and non-cancellable commitments incurred for the January 2026 to October 2026 implementation timeline. Each party will return or securely destroy the other party's Confidential Information in accordance with the governing agreement, except for copies required for legal, regulatory, or backup purposes. Termination does not affect accrued payment obligations, confidentiality, intellectual property rights, audit rights, limitation of liability, indemnities, or any provision intended to survive termination.
